questions.question: Which of the following statements describes “endemic species”?

options.text: Species with less population may move to the category of endangered species.
Species that are not found existing after intense searches.
Species that are found only in some particular areas.
Species that have come from abroad.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **3 **i.e __**Species that are found only in some particular areas.**__

 
• Species that are found only in some particular areas are called endemic species.
 
• Endemic species can easily become extinct or endangered from the earth.
 
• **The dodo** is an extinct flightless bird that was endemic to the island of Mauritius, in the Indian ocean.
 
• Dodo is an example of the vulnerability of endemic species to habitat alteration.
 
• Important Endemic specie in India are:
 
 
• Asiatic Lion in Gir Forest.
 
• Nilgiri Tahr in Nilgiri Hills.
 
• Sangai Deer in Loktak Lake.
 
• Purple Frog in the Western Ghats.
 
• Kashmir Stag in Kashmir Valley.
 
• Lion Tailed Macaque in the Western Ghats.
 
• Pygmy Hog in Assam.
 
• Malabar Civet in the Western Ghats.

questions.question: From which country did the Indian Constitution borrow the idea of directive principles of state policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **4** i.e __**Ireland.**__

 
• Indian Constitution borrowed the idea of directive principles of state policy from Ireland.
 
 
• The makers of the Constitution of India were influenced by the Irish **Home Rule Movement** and other national movements of Ireland. 
 
• **Part IV **of the Indian constitution deals with the directive principles of state policy.
 
• Directive principles of state policy(DPSP) deal with economic and cultural rights.
 
• Directive Principles of state policy(DPSP) are **non-justiciable.**
 
• Directive principles of state policy aims at the establishment of the welfare state.
 
 
 
• Important features in the Indian constitution borrowed from **Ireland** are:
 
 
• The nomination of members to Rajya Sabha
 
• Presidetnial election.
 
• Directive principles of state policy
 
 
 
• Important features in the Indian constitution borrow from **Germany** is:
 
 
• Suspension of Fundamental Rights during the emergency.
 
 
 
• Important features in the Indian constitution borrow from** South Africa** are:
 
 
• Amendment to the Constitution.
 
• Election of members of Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• Important features in the Indian constitution borrow from **Britain** are:
 
 
• Parliamentary form of government.
 
• Office of Comptroller and Auditor General.
 
• Rule of Law.
 
• Legislative procedure.
 
• Single Citizenship.
 
• Cabinet system.
 
• Writs.

questions.question: Which one of the following waves are used by the common TV remote control?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **4** i.e __**Infrared waves.**__

 
• Infrared wave is an electromagnetic wave.
 
 
• It was discovered by William Herschel.
 
• Infrared waves are used by the common **TV remote control.**
 
• Waves used in distant photography.
 
• Invisible to the human eye.
 
• Most of the thermal radiation emitted by objects near room temperature is infrared.
 
• Used for target acquisition purposes in military and civilian applications.
 
• Wavelength:** 700 nanometers to 1 millimeter.**
 
• The **heat of the sunlight **is due to Infrared rays.
 
 

 
 

 Radio waves
 
 
 
• Electromagnetic wave with** maximum wavelength.**
 
• Wavelength: 1 meter to 100,000 km.
 
• Waves used in radio and television broadcasting.
 
• Radio waves were first predicted by** James Clerk Maxwell.**
 
 
 
 

 Lasers
 
 
 
• LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.
 
• Source of intense monochromatic light.
 
• Discovered by** Theodore Maiman.**
 
• Used in medical fields to perform minute operations.
 
 
 
 

 Ultrasonic waves
 
 
 
• Sound waves **produced by Bats.**
 
• Sound higher than 20000 Hz.
 
• Inaudible sound for humans.
 
• Used in ultrasound scanning.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution provides powers to the president of India to declare National emergency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **3** i.e __**Article 352.**__

 
• The President of India is empowered to proclaim three types of emergencies to handle extraordinary situations in the country
 
 
• The three types of emergencies in India are namely:
 
 
• National Emergency.
 
• State Emergency.
 
• Financial Emergency.
 
 
 
• President can proclaim a **National Emergency** under** Article 352 **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• President can proclaim National Emergency only after receiving a written **recommendation from the cabinet.**
 
• The proclamation must be approved by both houses of the Parliament within one month.
 
• It can be continued for six months with a special majority.
 
• **The first National Emergency In India **was proclaimed by Dr. S Radhakrishnan on 26th October 1962.
 
 
• The first National Emergency was due to Chinese aggression.
 
• It was revoked by Zakir Hussain on 10th January 1968.
 
 
 
• **The Second National Emergency** In India was proclaimed by V V Giri on 3rd December 1971.
 
• **The Third National Emergency **In India was proclaimed by Fakrudin Ali Ahmad on 25th June 1975.
 
• Both the Second and Third National Emergencies were revoked by B. D Jetty.
 
 
 
• **Article 356** deals with the commencement of **President Rule** in a state.
 
• **Article 371** deals with the Special provision to the Maharashtra and Gujarat states.

questions.question: As per the text ‘Charaka Samhita’ how many bones are there in a human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **2** i.e __**360.**__

 
• The Charaka Saṃhita is a famous Sanskrit text on Ayurveda medicine.
 
 
• It was authored by **Maharshi Charaka.**
 
• The Charaka Samhita mentioned that the content of the book was first taught by **Atreya Punarvasu.**
 
• It is one of the foundational Hindu texts of medicines that have survived from ancient India.
 
• As per the text ‘Charaka Samhita’ there are 360 bones in a human body.
 
• Charaka studied the anatomy of the human body and concluded that there are **360 bones including teeth, present in the human body.**
 
• As per the text Charaka Samhita, there are four important parts of medical practice:
 
 
• The patient.
 
• The physician.
 
• The nurse.
 
• The medicines.
 
 
 
 
 
• Human body composed of around **270 bones by birth**.
 
• The number of bones will be reduced to around** 206 bones by adulthood** after some bones get fused together.

questions.question: A solution of which of the following is needed to test the presence of proteins?

options.text: Copper sulphate and caustic soda solution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper Sulphate and caustic soda solution.**__

 
• Copper Sulphate and caustic soda solution are used to test the presence of proteins.
 
• The** biuret test **is used to confirm the presence of proteins in food materials.
 
• If the mixture turns** violet colour** that indicates the presence of proteins in the food.
 
• Other tests for protein detection are: 
 
 
• Xanthoproteic test.
 
• Millions test.
 
• Ninhydrin test.
 
 
 
• **Caustic soda **is also known as Sodium hydroxide.
 
 
• Formula: NaOH.
 
• Sodium hydroxide is used in the manufacture of pulp and paper, soaps, and detergents.
 
 
 
• **Copper Sulphate** is also called blue vitriol.
 
 
• Formula: CuSO₄.
 
• It is used as an analytical reagent.
 
 
 
• **Iodine solution** is used for the test of Starch.
